message.content: The debug probe (t19) shows my poison helper was the problem: I poisoned pages per-batch, so pages unused by batch 0 (but used by batch 1) got NaN and tripped `validate_inputs` on batch 1's live slots. That's a probe bug, not kernel behavior. I'll rerun the NaN-poisoning probe with a globally-computed reachable set across all batches.

function.arguments:
{"claim_id": "c2", "code": "import sys, torch, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_115")
import kernel
dev="cuda"

def build(seed, window):
    g=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    b,qt,d,hk,page=2,9,64,2,16
    hq=4; lengths=[97,113]; pages=20; c=8
    q=(2*torch.rand((b,qt,hq,d),generator=g)-1).half()
    k=(2*torch.rand((pages,page,hk,d),generator=g)-1).half()
    v=(2*torch.rand(k.shape,generator=g)-1).half()
    tbl=torch.randint(0,pages,(b,c),generator=g).to(torch.int32)
    ln=torch.tensor(lengths,dtype=torch.int32)
    return tuple(t.to(dev) for t in (q,k,v,tbl,ln))+(window,)

def poison(k,v,q,tbl,ln,window):
    k=k.clone(); v=v.clone()
    b,qt,hq,d=q.shape
    page,hk=k.shape[1],k.shape[2]
    # reachable physical slots, union over ALL batches
    reachable=set()
    for i in range(b):
        length=int(ln[i].item())
        lo = max(0, length-qt-window+1) if window else 0
        for t in range(lo,length):
            reachable.add((i,int(tbl[i,t//page].item()),t%page))
    used=set(p for (i,p,pos) in reachable)
    for p in range(k.shape[0]):
        if p not in used:
            k[p]=float('nan'); v[p]=float('nan')
    for p in used:
        for pos in range(page):
            if not any((i,p2,pos)==(i,p,pos) for (i,p2,pos) in reachable if p2==p):
                k[p,pos]=float('nan'); v[p,pos]=float('nan')
    tbl=tbl.clone()
    for i in range(b):
        need=(int(ln[i].item())+page-1)//page
        tbl[i,need:]=999999
    return k,v,tbl

cases=[]
for seed,window in [(3,41),(4,0),(5,256),(6,1),(7,17)]:
    q,k,v,tbl,ln,window=build(seed,window)
    out_clean=kernel.run(q,k,v,tbl,ln,window)
    ref=kernel.reference(q,k,v,tbl,ln,window)
    ratio_clean=float(((out_clean.double()-ref).abs()/(0.003+0.003*ref.abs())).max())
    kp,vp,tblp=poison(k,v,q,tbl,ln,window)
    out_p=kernel.run(q,kp,vp,tblp,ln,window)
    finite=bool(torch.isfinite(out_p).all())
    diff=float((out_p.float()-out_clean.float()).abs().max())
    ratio_p=float(((out_p.double()-ref).abs()/(0.003+0.003*ref.abs())).max()) if finite else None
    cases.append([seed,window,round(ratio_clean,4),(round(ratio_p,4) if ratio_p is not None else None),round(diff,6),finite])
print(json.dumps({"metric":"contract ratio clean vs NaN-poisoned irrelevant slots (incl. dirty block_table entries beyond ceil(length/page))","reason":"irrelevant-slot NaN must not change output; require finite outputs and ratio<=1","cases":cases,"all_finite":all(c[5] for c in cases)}))", "expected_signal": "all cases finite, ratio_p <= 1, diff ~ 0"}

message.reasoning_content:
The debug probe shows no live-but-would-poison slots for window=41, so the earlier failure was from a different window case. The poison predicate uses reachable=positions in [lo,length) — but validate_inputs checks isfinite over positions lo..length which matches... Actually validate checks `lo = max(0, length - qt - window + 1)` and positions arange(lo, length) — same set. But live check is `cache[mapped, positions % page]` — for repeated page IDs, a physical slot (p,pos) may be reachable via multiple logical positions. My poison predicate keeps slot (p,pos) only if some reachable t maps to (p,pos) — same thing. Hmm, but wait: mapping is per batch. In batch 1, a page might be used; in batch 0 poisoned. validate checks per batch... should be fine.

Actually the earlier t18 failure: poisoning whole pages for pages not used by either batch? I used `used_pages` per batch i, poisoning pages not used in batch i — but the loop poisons in batch-0 iteration pages not used by batch 0, which may be used by batch 1! validate for batch 1 then sees NaN in a live slot. That's the bug in my probe: poison must be global over all batches' reachable sets.

Also note the kernel's own design: the kernel reads tiles up to max_prefix over all tiles (tile bounds include window filtering), and masked-out slots with scores=-inf get probability exp(-inf)=0, then accumulator += p*v → 0*NaN = NaN! Actually tl.where already zeroes scores; probabilities for disallowed positions are exp(-inf - max)=0, then tl.dot(probabilities, v) — dot product of zero with NaN gives NaN? 0*NaN = NaN in the accumulation. That's a genuine risk. But loads use mask tile_mask (logical < max_prefix) — positions beyond max_prefix get other=0.0. Positions within max_prefix but not allowed (window-expired) still load actual values (possibly NaN), and probabilities there are 0. dot(0 probabilities, NaN v) → NaN in accumulator. So c2 might actually be a real bug! Also tile_start/tile_end window bounds skip fully-expired tiles, but partial tiles contain expired positions.

So I must run the corrected poison probe. Also line 70-71: with window, v is zeroed via tl.where((context+qpos_lo - logical) < WINDOW, v, 0.0) — that zeroing handles NaN? tl.where(cond, v, 0.0) — NaN v where cond true stays NaN; cond true means within window of qpos_lo (lowest query), positions within window are reachable, so fine. Positions outside get 0.0, replacing NaN. But that where happens only when WINDOW>0. For window=0, no such zeroing, and probabilities are 0 for disallowed... but with window=0 all positions ≤ a are allowed, and positions beyond a within tile have probabilities 0 multiplying actual v values which are reachable by later queries (finite). So no NaN. For window>0, the where zeroes expired v — but only relative to qpos_lo. Positions expired for qpos_lo are expired for all q. So OK. But dot with probability 0 * v(NaN for unallocated pages within max_prefix tile range? Those positions have tile_mask true only if logical < max_prefix, and they load v even if unallocated... but they map via block_table valid entries < ceil(length/page)? logical < max_prefix ≤ length so page entry valid. So v values are within written area... "unwritten tail slots" beyond length within the last page: logical<length ensures written. Hmm — but positions between a+1 and length-1 (future relative to a query but written) are fine values.

Key NaN risk: probabilities=0 for disallowed positions in a tile whose v contains NaN. When can a loaded v slot be NaN and probability 0? Probability is 0 for logical positions > a (future) or outside window. Future positions < length are live (finite per contract only if reachable by some allowed position — future positions are not reachable for this query but may be reachable for later queries; the last query's allowed set covers up to length-1... but positions > a of the last query don't exist. For query r=QT-1, a=length-1, all t<length allowed. So all t<length are reachable by the final query, hence live. Positions ≥ length aren't loaded (mask). Window-expired positions: allowed set of any query includes a_window... reachable = positions in [length-Q-window+1, length). Expired positions t < that lo may be NaN! And in a partial tile containing both expired and live positions, probabilities for expired are 0. The line 70-71 where-zeroing handles WINDOW>0 only for condition (context + qpos_lo - logical) < WINDOW, i.e., logical > context+qpos_lo-WINDOW = length-Q-WINDOW → exactly the reachable lo. So expired v slots get zeroed. Good — the kernel handles this.

But wait, probabilities.to(v.dtype) — v may have been zeroed. Fine.

What about k NaN: scores = SCALE*dot(q,k) with k NaN → NaN scores; then tl.where(mask, scores, -inf) — mask false gives -inf, but mask true with NaN score gives NaN → maximum NaN → everything NaN. When can a loaded k slot be NaN with allowed mask true? allowed requires logical ≤ a and within window; such positions are reachable → finite. When allowed false but tile_mask true, where gives -inf. So k NaN in disallowed positions is replaced by -inf. OK.

But: is k loaded with mask=tile_mask only (logical < max_prefix)? Disallowed but < max_prefix positions load NaN k, but where() replaces with -inf. Good. Similarly probabilities 0 * NaN v in dot → NaN in accumulator! Even though scores are -inf → probabilities 0, the accumulator += tl.dot(0, NaN_v) = NaN. Unless line 70-71 zeroes v. With WINDOW>0, expired positions zeroed. With WINDOW=0, disallowed = only future positions (logical > a), which are live. So no NaN v among probability-0 positions with window=0. Hmm — but what about rows where qpos >= QT (padding rows)? Those rows' outputs are masked at store. Fine.

Also, when WINDOW>0, but tile range: tile_start skips fully-expired tiles. Within included tiles, expired positions exist — zeroed by line 70. Good. But there's a subtlety: line 70 uses qpos_lo = qb*BQ, the block's lowest query. Zeroing v where (context+qpos_lo-logical) >= WINDOW. That's per whole block of queries (BM rows all from same qb? rows=0..BM-1, qpos = qb*BQ + rows//GROUP — since BM=BQ*GROUP, yes all rows in [qb*BQ, qb*BQ+BQ)). OK.

So the kernel looks correctly designed. My probe just needs the cross-batch fix. Run it.
